script.title: Lincoln Spoke 271 Words After a Two-Hour Speech
sentences: The star speaker at Gettysburg talked for two hours.
It was November 19, 1863, and about 15,000 people came to dedicate a cemetery.
The other guest was only asked for a few appropriate remarks.
He'd felt weak on the train, and dizzy that morning.
An aide wrote that his face had a ghastly color.
Abraham Lincoln stood up and spoke 271 words in about two minutes.
Heading home he was feverish, and was later diagnosed with mild smallpox.
Everett's speech is seldom read now; Lincoln's opens with four score and seven years ago.
scenes: Extreme close-up of orator Edward Everett's face in 1863, white hair, mid-speech, eyes blazing with passion, mouth open, a crowd blurred behind him under a grey November sky.
About fifteen thousand people in 1863 coats and bonnets gathered on the rolling fields of Gettysburg around a wooden platform, flags and new cemetery rows, overcast November light, wide aerial shot.
Edward Everett in a black frock coat, gesturing grandly at a podium, many handwritten pages in his hand, the crowd shifting restlessly, long shadows of afternoon, medium shot.
Abraham Lincoln in his black suit and stovepipe hat sitting quietly on the platform, reading a single folded sheet of paper, modest expression, cold grey light, medium shot.
Abraham Lincoln sitting pale and tired in a swaying 1863 railroad car, one hand on his forehead, window light flickering, the countryside passing, medium close-up.
Abraham Lincoln's gaunt face looking greyish and ill as a young aide watches him with concern, a hotel room in Gettysburg, dim morning light, close medium shot.
Abraham Lincoln standing tall at the platform with one short page, speaking solemnly to the silent crowd, cemetery and fields behind, a shaft of light breaking through clouds, low-angle shot.
Abraham Lincoln slumped in a train seat wrapped in a shawl, feverish and weak, a worried aide beside him, dim lamp-lit railroad car at dusk, medium shot.
Abraham Lincoln's solemn profile beside the Gettysburg cemetery at sunset, rows of white headstones and a flag, quiet reverent mood, golden light, wide shot.
script.description:
On November 19, 1863, the main speech at Gettysburg lasted two hours.
Lincoln's came after it: 271 words, from a man about to be diagnosed with smallpox.
claims_en: Edward Everett's oration, the main speech of the day at Gettysburg, lasted two hours
It was the dedication of Soldiers' National Cemetery on the grounds where the battle was fought
Everett's speech was 13,607 words and was well received by the crowd
Lincoln was invited to set apart the grounds with 'a few appropriate remarks' after the oration
Lincoln told John Hay during the trip on November 18 that he felt weak, and told Nicolay the next morning he felt dizzy
Hay noted that Lincoln's face had 'a ghastly color'
Lincoln's speech was 271 words and lasted about two minutes
After the speech, on the train back, Lincoln was feverish and weak; he was later diagnosed with a mild case of smallpox
Everett's speech is now seldom read
Lincoln's speech begins 'Four score and seven years ago'
